reason: The cited evidence shows that thermal aging at 700°C causes softening, not toughening, in TiVNbTa (E1, E3, E4), and that high-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi (E5, E6, E7), but no evidence links this transition to improved toughness, nor does any evidence combine thermal aging and high-strain compression or demonstrate the mechanism across both alloy systems.
premises: Thermal aging at 700°C causes phase segregation and softening in TiVNbTa due to interstitial depletion
High-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi
The combined effects of thermal aging and high-strain compression will produce a clustering-to-ordering transition
The proposed mechanism applies to both TiVNbTa and Al0.1CrCoFeNi alloy systems
